added_models.model: Safety-pharmacology core battery: hERG patch-clamp and single-dose conscious-dog cardiovascular telemetry (vepdegestrant)

safety.confidence_note: FDA-authored nonclinical assessment summarising the sponsor's safety-pharmacology reports, which were not read. The studies were run pre-IND (unpublished), so 2026 is a proxy first-use year; the class's GDC-0810-era hERG data were not found in print.
safety.note: Vepdegestrant's ICH S7 battery: hERG negative to 30 µM (>1000x free Cmax), single-dose dog telemetry clean at 400 mg/kg; no CV liability predicted.
safety.short: hERG and dog telemetry predict no CV effect
safety.quote: Vepdegestrant had no effect on hERG tail current at concentrations up to 30 µM (the limit of solubility) when compared with vehicle-treated cells.
safety.judgement: Opened as its own track: the standalone safety-pharmacology battery (in-vitro hERG plus single-dose telemetry) is a different system from the repeat-dose rat/dog toxicology track and made the opposite prediction (no cardiovascular effect) from the repeat-dose dog ECG (QT/QTc/PR prolongation).

safety.magnitude_basis: hERG no effect to 30 µM (>1000x free Cmax) and single-dose dog telemetry clean at 400 mg/kg (10x free Cmax) versus patient mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms (90% CI 8.2-13.6), label section 5.1 QTc warning
safety.confidence_note: Both sides are in the same FDA review (nonclinical section lines ~1882-1888; clinical section line ~1064) but the review never reconciles them, so this is a pairing I made, hatched. The 10-fold dog margin is on free Cmax; the dog study is single-dose, so a repeat-dose effect was outside what it could show, yet the hERG result at >1000x free Cmax is a direct miss. Registry date is the VERITAC-2 (NCT05654623) results posting.
safety.note: Patients on 200 mg showed mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms, 11% TdP/QT SMQ events vs 1% on fulvestrant, and a label QTc warning; none predicted.
safety.short: Clean hERG and dog telemetry, patients prolonged QTc
safety.quote: Notably, vepdegestrant is associated with QTc prolongation (mean ΔQTcF: 10.9 msec [90% CI: 8.2 to 13.6 msec]).
safety.reason: hERG, dog telemetry clean; patients prolonged QTc
safety.judgement: Contra, not pooled into the repeat-dose track's same/partial: the run's track-identity rule keeps a different model with a different prediction apart, and the count-once rule is satisfied because the repeat-dose dog track already carries the harm as predicted; this track records the component that predicted wrongly. Magnitude direction_only, as other hERG/telemetry misses in the atlas; the review does not call it, so source_calls_it is null.

added_models.model: Zebrafish embryo heart-rate model of SERD-induced bradycardia (wild-type and esr1/esr2/gper mutants)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC; the paper is open access but the figures were not opened). First use of this system for the class is this paper.
safety.note: Zebrafish embryos dosed with oral SERDs to explain the bradycardia seen with giredestrant and camizestrant in trials; built after the clinical signal.
safety.short: Zebrafish model built for SERD bradycardia
safety.quote: To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanism, we used chemical biology and genetic approaches in a zebrafish model of SERD-induced bradycardia.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for a retrodiction model: the clinical bradycardia (giredestrant dose-related heart-rate fall, phase Ia/b) was known before the model was built, so any match can only score retro.

safety.magnitude_basis: presence or absence of bradycardia per SERD in zebrafish embryos versus clinical reports: giredestrant and camizestrant positive, amcenestrant and fulvestrant negative in both
safety.confidence_note: Patient side is as the paper states it (giredestrant bradycardia from its phase Ia/b and C-QTc reports; amcenestrant none in AMEERA trials); the trial papers were not re-read for heart-rate tables. Camizestrant is not a member and does not score.
safety.note: Giredestrant slowed zebrafish hearts and amcenestrant did not, matching which members cause bradycardia in patients; esr1 mutants were protected, so on-target.
safety.quote: Giredestrant and camizestrant induced significant bradycardia in wild-type zebrafish embryos, whereas fulvestrant and amcenestrant (SERDs that do not induce bradycardia in patients) did not alter heart rate.
safety.reason: Reproduced which SERDs slow the heart
safety.judgement: Retro, not same: the model was run after the clinic knew the answer (decision 10). Scored on the two members it dosed (giredestrant positive, amcenestrant negative), both reproduced; the esr1-mutant rescue adds mechanism (on-target ER signalling) that the repeat-dose rat/dog track never offered. Class-level: it separates molecules, not patients.

added_models.model: Bottom-up translational PBPK (IVIVE from rat/mouse ADME) predicting human vepdegestrant PK

dose.confidence_note: Open-access paper (PMC12151198); methods and figure legends read, not the supplementary tables. Online 2024-12-28, print May 2025.
dose.note: [14C]vepdegestrant rat ADME and hepatocyte IVIVE fed a GastroPlus PBPK model built to simulate human plasma concentration-time profiles.
dose.short: Rat ADME-based PBPK built to predict human PK
dose.quote: was synthesized as a model PROTAC to characterize its preclinical ADME properties and simulate its clinical pharmacokinetics (PK) by establishing a physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK) model.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first public use of a preclinical-to-human PBPK for a member drug; the human 30 mg PK was already known from phase 1, so what follows is a retrodiction.

dose.magnitude_basis: simulated versus observed human plasma concentration-time profile after 30 mg oral (figure overlay; no human fold-error stated; rat PBPK within 1.75-fold)
dose.confidence_note: Retrodiction: the observed 30 mg human data are the published phase 1 profile (source of the observed data, patients vs volunteers, not stated in the sections read, so subjects is null). No fold error is given for the human simulation, so magnitude is null.
dose.note: The in-vitro-ADME-informed human PBPK overlaid the observed 30 mg plasma profile; rat model within 1.75-fold of observed across fed and fasted states.
dose.short: Human 30 mg profile reproduced from preclinical ADME
dose.quote: Human models, informed by in vitro ADME data, closely mirrored postoral dose plasma profiles at 30 mg.
dose.judgement: Retro (decision 10): model built after the human PK was public and reproduced it. Dose cell because the prediction is the exposure a given dose produces; the model made no efficacy claim.

dose.magnitude_basis: refined PBPK-simulated versus observed human oral PK across 60-360 mg vepdegestrant; the initial bottom-up prediction over-predicted CL/F at 30 mg
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; paywalled. Online 2025-12-24 (ArticleDate), print February 2026. The pure bottom-up prediction missed clearance, which is why source_calls_it is partial rather than match; the refined model is a fit to the observed data.
dose.note: A second group's mouse-informed PBPK (Simcyp-style IVIVE) over-predicted CL/F at 30 mg bottom-up, then matched 60-360 mg within 2-fold after one clearance scalar.
dose.quote: The refined PBPK models successfully simulated human oral PK within 2-fold of observed values across multiple doses (60-360 mg for ARV-471 and 70-140 mg for ARV-110).
dose.reason: Human PK reproduced within 2-fold, after refinement
dose.judgement: Same track as the 2024 entry: same system (preclinical-ADME-driven PBPK of vepdegestrant) making the same prediction (human exposure per dose), so it strengthens rather than opens a track. Still retro because the human data were in hand.

added_models.model: Sponsor Simcyp PBPK model of vepdegestrant/ARV-473 for CYP3A drug-drug interactions and organ impairment (filed in NDA 219835)

dose.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review appendix 19.4.3 (Applicant's position and FDA assessment). Simcyp v23 dates the build to about 2023-24; 2026 is the first public date, used as a proxy first-use year.
dose.note: Sponsor's Simcyp v23 PBPK of vepdegestrant and its epimer, built from in-vitro ADME/DDI parameters to predict CYP3A interactions and organ-impairment exposure.
dose.short: Simcyp PBPK filed for DDI predictions
dose.quote: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was developed and verified for vepdegestrant and its epimer ARV-473 using the Simcyp® Simulator (version 23) software platform.
dose.judgement: Separate from the translational PBPK track: a different model (clinically anchored, DDI-oriented, sponsor-filed) with a different prediction (interaction ratios and impairment exposure, not first-in-human PK).

dose.magnitude_basis: ratio of predicted to observed AUC and Cmax (single- and multiple-dose PK) and AUCR/CmaxR (itraconazole, carbamazepine, midazolam DDI studies) within 0.80-1.25
dose.confidence_note: Applicant-authored sentence; the FDA's own assessment reads 'The Applicant's PBPK modeling is adequate to predict the effects of CYP3A percipients on vepdegestrant exposure' but called its hepatic-impairment use 'not mature' and required a PMR clinical study for moderate CYP3A inhibitors, so reliance is partial. Subjects mixed: DDI studies in healthy participants, multiple-dose PK in patients. Registry dates of the DDI studies not looked up.
dose.note: Predicted-to-observed ratios for PK and the itraconazole, carbamazepine and midazolam DDI studies fell within 0.80-1.25; FDA accepted it for CYP3A perpetrators and CYP2B6/UGT1A9 label statements.
dose.short: PBPK verified on clinical DDI, used in label
dose.quote: the ratio of predicted to observed (RP/O) for vepdegestrant and ARV-473 AUC and Cmax values in PK studies and AUCR and CmaxR values in DDI studies fell within a predictive performance criterion of 0.80 to 1.25
dose.reason: Verified on clinical DDI; label leans on it
dose.judgement: Retro: verification against completed clinical PK/DDI studies is a retrodiction by definition; the prospective predictions it then made (bupropion 1.44x, dapagliflozin 1.55x, organ impairment ≤1.28x) were accepted without a clinical check, so they have no patient comparison and open no further entry. Regulator acceptance of in-silico data for label text is noted here but the context-level regulatory_reliance flag is the draft's call.

added_models.model: EpiIntestinal human primary intestinal 3D microtissue with PBPK (transporter DDI prediction)

dose.population: healthy participants in vepdegestrant DDI studies; ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer indication
dose.confidence_note: Open-access paper (PMC12641084); results section on vepdegestrant read. model_kind ex_vivo because the tissue is primary human intestinal cells; the enum has no in-vitro value.
dose.note: Human primary intestinal 3D microtissue assessed for predicting absorption, CYP3A induction and transporter DDIs, with vepdegestrant as the P-gp/BCRP perpetrator case.
dose.short: Human gut microtissue tested as DDI predictor
dose.quote: This study aims to comprehensively assess the EpiIntestinal™, a human primary intestinal 3D model, for its ability to predict oral absorption (Fa), intestinal availability (Fg), CYP3A4 induction, and drug-drug interactions (DDIs).
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the clinical DDI results it tests against (NCT05673889 dabigatran, NCT05652660 rosuvastatin) were complete before the assay was run, so the comparison is a retrodiction.

dose.magnitude_basis: dabigatran etexilate absorptive Papp +2.6-fold with vepdegestrant in EpiIntestinal versus clinical Cmax +2.9-fold (paper; FDA review gives Cmax +92%, AUC +98%); rosuvastatin Papp +48% versus clinical Cmax +11%
dose.population: healthy participants in vepdegestrant DDI studies; ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer indication
dose.confidence_note: The paper's 2.9-fold dabigatran Cmax cites the registry record; the FDA review reports +92% Cmax, so the clinical anchor is itself uncertain by ~1.5x; the model's 2.6-fold is within 2x of either. Healthy-volunteer subjects inferred from the Pfizer DDI study design (the itraconazole study in the review enrolled healthy adults); the two registry records were not opened, registry_date null.
dose.note: Vepdegestrant raised dabigatran Papp 2.6-fold in the microtissue vs 2.9-fold clinical Cmax, and rosuvastatin 48% vs 11% clinical; Caco-2 over-predicted both (6-fold, 127%).
dose.short: Gut microtissue matched vepdegestrant transporter DDIs
dose.quote: Additionally, the model accurately predicted clinical outcomes of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) mediated DDIs for ARV-471.
dose.judgement: Retro: run after the clinical DDI studies and reproduced them in direction and within 2-fold. Dose cell because the prediction is co-medication exposure under vepdegestrant, as the atlas scores PBPK DDI tracks elsewhere; it says nothing about vepdegestrant's own efficacy or exposure target. Caco-2, compared in the same paper and over-predicting, is not added as a track (see considered_not_added).

considered_not_added: persevERA (NCT04546009; Roche release 2026-03-09, ITT PFS not met): a patient-side result for the existing er-pos-wt-breast-xenograft efficacy track, which is already contra; belongs in that entry's patient_trials (tier 5, trial_unreported), not a new system. The draft is not edited by this task.

ZN-c5 discontinuation (Zentalis, August 2022, no randomised readout): no model-patient comparison exists; its own preclinical systems (MCF7 wild-type and ESR1-mutant xenografts, J Med Chem 2025 PMID 40654307; Mol Cancer Ther 2026 PMID 41383111) are the two xenograft tracks the draft already has.

Patient-derived organoids: no organoid work with any member drug (PubMed 1 hit, a PROTAC review; Europe PMC hits are reviews); organoid-to-clinic concordance exists only for fulvestrant regimens (non-member). No organoid track is missing.
Ex-vivo explants / CTC cultures / patient-derived cells: none with a member drug; the elacestrant fulvestrant-refractory CTC culture (PMID 37318638) is a non-member.

Giredestrant HCI-013 PBPK-PD tumour-growth-inhibition model projecting the human efficacious dose (Biopharm Drug Dispos 2023, PMID 37102506, doi 10.1002/bdd.2358): an in-silico dose-selection model for a member, but paywalled and the abstract states neither the projected dose nor a comparison with the 30 mg clinical dose; the Wiley page returned a bot wall. No quotable comparison, so not added; would be a dose track if the full text is obtained.

Giredestrant dose-selection rationale (Expert Opin Investig Drugs 2026, PMID 41610202): narrative account that 'preclinical and phase I/II' data informed the 30 mg dose; paywalled; no model number or comparison in the abstract.

Amcenestrant joint tumour-dynamics/PFS model (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2024, PMID 38558299): built on 75 AMEERA-1/2 patients and evaluated against AMEERA-3's amcenestrant-arm PFS after that trial read out; a clinical pharmacometric model with no preclinical input, so not a model system for this atlas. It would be an in_silico efficacy retro if patient-data models are admitted.

Vepdegestrant population PK / exposure-response (J Clin Pharmacol 2026, PMID 42572241; FDA review 19.4.1-19.4.2) and concentration-QTc analyses (FDA review; giredestrant Clin Transl Sci 2023, PMID 36772881): analyses of patient data, not model systems.

Giredestrant, amcenestrant and brilanestrant safety-pharmacology (hERG, dog telemetry): no public model-side data (giredestrant unapproved, no FDA review; Liang 2021 abstract's 'excellent in vitro and in vivo safety profiles' already anchors the rat/dog track), so the hERG/telemetry track carries vepdegestrant only.

Caco-2 permeability assay (compared in the same EpiIntestinal paper): over-predicted vepdegestrant's transporter DDIs (dabigatran Papp 6-fold vs 2.9-fold clinical; rosuvastatin +127% vs +11%); a generic screening assay not used to carry the class into patients, so not opened as its own track; noted in the EpiIntestinal entry.
Immature-rat uterotrophic assay (ER antagonism/no agonism in vivo, used in the class's discovery papers): no patient endometrial comparison in any source read; no dedicated search run.
